rem:gr-aether-geometry:
Remark General Relativity as the Aether Geometry. Gravity in this model emerges as the back-reaction of the gauge fields on the CR manifold M. The geometry curves to accommodate the tension of the \mathrm{SU}(2) instantons. The Levi form L_\varTheta and its coupling to the gauge curvature F_A replace the metric. The variational bicomplex on the infinite jet bundle organises this coupling. This bicomplex is the double complex (\Omega^{p,q}(J^\infty E), d_H, d_V). The horizontal differential d_H acts along the base M, while the vertical differential d_V acts along the fibre.

Variation of the action \mathfrak{S}_q with respect to the Levi form L_\varTheta yields the field equations:

  \frac{\delta \mathfrak{S}_q}{\delta L_\varTheta}
  =  0
  \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
  \mathrm{Ric}_{g_\varTheta} =  T^{(q)}.

Here \mathrm{Ric}_{g_\varTheta} denotes the Tanaka–Webster Ricci curvature and T^{(q)} denotes a q-weighted stress-energy 2-tensor on H. Both are coordinate-free objects.

The weight q(p). The q-weighted curvature–Levi functional couples the instanton energy to the aether by weighting the horizontal self-dual curvature by the local Levi-form magnitude q(p). Regions where F_A^+ overlaps the Levi form L_\varTheta contribute more strongly.
sec:symmetric-point-preamble: The mass-gap conjecture locates the vanishing of the gap on the 2-torsion locus \mu_2 = \{1, -1\} \subset \mathbb{G}_m. This section examines the symmetric point q = 1 directly. This section determines which structures of the mass tower \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n) survive the specialisation, which degenerate, and at what order in h = q - 1 each lost structure restores when the deformation switches back on. The pattern is uniform. The symmetric point deletes no spectrum, but loses resolution. Distinctions that braiding maintains—chirality of crossings, inter-nucleon channel identity, accidental level coincidences—collapse at q = 1 and reopen at definite infinitesimal orders.
prop:symmetric-point-channel-collapse:
Proposition Channel collapse at the symmetric point. At the symmetric point q = 1, the three Hecke channels \sigma, \sigma^{-1}, and (\sigma + \sigma^{-1})/2 degenerate to a single operator. The reason is a purely algebraic identity in any field.

Let R be a field with 2 \neq 0 and let s \in R satisfy s^2 = 1. Then s^{-1} = s, and consequently

  \frac{s + s^{-1}}{2} \;=\; s .
prf:symmetric-point-channel-collapse:
Proof Proof of symmetric point channel collapse. At the symmetric point the two Hecke channels \sigma and \sigma^{-1} become indistinguishable — their eigenvalues merge — so their symmetric average carries no more information than a single generator.

From s^2 = 1 the element s is invertible with s^{-1} = s. Substituting, (s + s^{-1})/2 = (s + s)/2 = s. \square

At q \neq 1 the eigenvalues of a Hecke generator are \{q, -q^{-1}\}, which are distinct and separate \sigma from \sigma^{-1}; at q = 1 they degenerate to \mu_2 = \{1, -1\} — the same 2-torsion locus on which the crossing-energy gap functional vanishes. The proposition is the algebraic core of every channel degeneration recorded in this section: whatever physical data is carried by the choice among \sigma, \sigma^{-1}, and their average is invisible at the symmetric point and is restored only at positive order in h = q - 1.
rem:symmetric-point-channel-collapse: Remark Channel collapse across all three operator assignments. Any family of operator assignments drawn from \{\sigma,\ \sigma^{-1},\ (\sigma + \sigma^{-1})/2\} collapses to a single operator under the specialisation q = 1 of the Hecke relation (\sigma - q)(\sigma + q^{-1}) = 0, which at q = 1 reads \sigma^2 = 1.
prop:physical-units-gap-linear:
Proposition The physically normalised gap vanishes linearly at q = 1. The observable gap and the categorical bound scale differently near the symmetric point q = 1. Expressing the gap in physical units divides the cubically-vanishing categorical bound by \hbar_q^{\,2}. This changes the vanishing order from cubic to linear.

Let q \in \mathbb{R} with q \neq 0, 1. Let \mathfrak{E}_\times(q) = \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}) be the crossing energy, and let \hbar_q = (q-1)/q. Then the crossing-energy gap bound \Delta_q = \mathfrak{E}_\times(q)\,(q-1)^2 satisfies the exact identity

  \frac{\Delta_q}{\hbar_q^{\,2}}
  \;=\;
  \frac{q\,(q-1)(q+1)}{2}.

The gap in physical units vanishes linearly in h = q - 1 as q \to 1. The categorical bound \Delta_q vanishes cubically. Both vanish identically at q = 1.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows treats q as a real physical scale near q = 1. Generic categorical identities drawn upon remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
prf:physical-units-gap-linear:
Proof Proof of physical units gap linear. The archimedean normalisation 1/\hbar_q^2 in the mass formula buys back exactly two of the three vanishing orders of \Delta_q, and no more. It separates two rates that are easily conflated, and leaves a physical-units mass gap at first order in h.

Direct computation: \Delta_q / \hbar_q^2 = \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1})(q-1)^2 \cdot q^2/(q-1)^2 = \tfrac{1}{2}\,q^2\,(q - q^{-1}) = \tfrac{1}{2}\,q\,(q^2 - 1). \square

A mass gap in physical units is therefore a first-order-in-h phenomenon, in agreement with the first-order Reeb coupling (1 - q^{-1}) of the categorical Dirac operator. The identity is verified numerically to fifty digits.
rem:symmetric-point-resolution-loss:
Remark The symmetric point loses resolution, not spectrum. The specialisation q = 1 deletes no part of the mass tower. The weight spectrum of \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n) remains semisimple. Every Plancherel weight w_\lambda(q) = [n]_q! \,/\, H_q(\lambda)^2 is strictly positive at q = 1 (the classical measure d_\lambda^2/n!). The symmetric point loses resolution in two graded ways, collected into a stratification.

Channel identity. By channel collapse, the three inter-nucleon assignments \sigma, \sigma^{-1}, (\sigma + \sigma^{-1})/2 coincide at q = 1. The distinctions carrying chirality and pairing data are invisible at the symmetric point.

Accidental degeneracy. At n = 6, the weight tower has six distinct levels for q \neq 1 but five at q = 1. The conjugate pair \{(5,1), (2,1^4)\} and the pair \{(3,3), (2,2,2)\} land on the common classical value 25/720. The deformation resolves an accidental coincidence of the symmetric group (d_{(5,1)} = d_{(3,3)} = 5) that the classical point cannot see. The splitting reopens at second order,

  w_{(3,3)}(1+\varepsilon) - w_{(5,1)}(1+\varepsilon)
  \;=\; \tfrac{5}{18}\,\varepsilon^2 + O(\varepsilon^3),

with the linear term excluded by the bar-invariance w_\lambda(q) = w_\lambda(q^{-1}).

The stratification. Collecting these rates with the gap orders of the linear-vanishing identity gives a uniform picture of the infinitesimal neighbourhood q = 1 + \varepsilon:

order surviving / reopening structure
\varepsilon^0 semisimple tower; classical Plancherel weights; vacuum level
\varepsilon^1 physically normalised mass gap \tfrac{1}{2}q(q-1)(q+1); Dirac–Reeb coupling (1 - q^{-1})
\varepsilon^2 degeneracy resolution (the n = 6 inter-nucleon channel splitting, coefficient 5/18)
\varepsilon^3 categorical gap bound \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1})(q-1)^2

Every structure survives the limit surreally—as a positive infinitesimal of definite order—while only the standard parts of the gap quantities vanish. The classical point is not an impoverished theory but an unresolved one. This is verified numerically to fifty digits.
rem:unit-circle-photonic-sector:
Remark Phase on the circle, mass off it. On the unit circle q = e^{i\theta}, the crossing energy is purely imaginary:

  \mathfrak{E}_\times(e^{i\theta})
  \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(e^{i\theta} - e^{-i\theta}\bigr)
  \;=\; i \sin\theta .

A crossing on |q| = 1 generates phase, not energy. The circle direction of \mathbb{G}_m carries interference and transport—the electrodynamic, photonic sector. Real, positive crossing energy requires leaving the circle (q \in \mathbb{R}, q > 1). The two real points \mu_2 = \{1, -1\}, where the circle meets the real axis, are doubly degenerate. There, both the phase resolution and the mass scale vanish at once.

The categorical Dirac operator realises the same split internally. Its deviation from the bare connection is the Reeb-direction coupling weighted by (1 - q^{-1}), which vanishes at q = 1 and is first order in h = q - 1. This is the same order at which the physically normalised gap opens. Mass is a first-order radial phenomenon on \mathbb{G}_m. Electrodynamics is the angular phase flow that survives on the circle.

At the fibre level, the deformation parameter remains a formal, possibly complex variable. The archimedean evaluation selects a real q_0 > 1 and thereby a massive sector. Massless (photonic) content belongs on |q| = 1. Any chiral or massive content requires |q| \neq 1.
sec:archimedean-models-intro:
Over \mathbb{R} and \mathbb{C}, the aether parameter q varies smoothly, and the categorical axioms take the form of differential geometry on a contact three-manifold. Every Archimedean quantum observable universe is realized as a \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})-bundle over a strictly pseudoconvex CR base equipped with an \mathrm{SU}(2) frame.

Four explicit geometric constructions illustrate the scope of the Archimedean axioms:

  • Calabi–Yau hypersurfaces: a real hypersurface in a K3 surface inherits a strictly pseudoconvex CR structure whose contact data recovers classical instanton moduli.
  • Asymptotically locally Euclidean (ALE) spaces: resolution of aKleinian quotient \mathbb{C}^2/\Gamma yields an ADE orbifold whose tautological bundles realize the McKay correspondence.
  • The unit circle bundle over Bring's surface: the Seifert fibration over the genus-four curve \Sigma_4 (\chi(\Sigma_4) = -6) produces the canonical five-fold symmetric fibre geometry.
  • Cosmological endpoints: the limiting regimes q \to 1 and q \to \infty isolate the classical symmetric limit and the deep-quantum saturation boundary.

Invariants of an Archimedean model arise from two complementary sources. The principal bundle supplies gauge-theoretic data—the instanton connection, irreducibility criteria, self-dual curvature, and the Seiberg–Witten differential—while the Reeb fibre supplies contact-geometric data through the Levi form, the Tanaka–Webster metric, and the q-deformed Heisenberg commutator. A spatial-realization functor intertwines these two descriptions and matches the categorical action against the classical Chern–Simons functional before the subsequent section transports the construction to \mathbb{Q}_p.
ex:calabi-yau:
Example Real hypersurface in a Calabi--Yau 2-fold. Classical hyper-Kähler geometry provides a natural setting for quantum observable universes.

Let X be a Calabi–Yau 2-fold (a K3 surface) with holonomy \mathrm{SU}(2). Let M \subset X be a smooth, strictly convex real hypersurface. The ambient Kähler geometry induces a 3-dimensional strictly pseudoconvex CR structure on M. The frame bundle of X restricts to a principal \mathrm{SU}(2)-bundle P \to M over the hypersurface. The associated state bundle \mathcal{S} = P \times_{\mathrm{SU}(2)} \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) completes the data for an archimedean quantum observable universe.

Because X is hyper-Kähler, the Kähler potential induces a contact form \varTheta on M. The Reeb vector field \xi is the restriction of the Hamiltonian vector field of the Kähler potential. The hyper-Kähler triple (\omega_I, \omega_J, \omega_K) restricts to forms on M, inducing the weight decomposition.

The categorical instanton condition reduces to the anti-self-duality equation F_A^+ = 0 on X. The moduli space of solutions is the classical instanton moduli space on a K3 surface. The aether parameter q(p) interpolates between this instanton connection and the Reeb component.

This construction casts standard instanton moduli problems as special cases of the categorical framework.
ex:ale:
Example ALE links. The links of ALE spaces provide a discrete, ADE-indexed family of archimedean quantum observable universes.

Let \Gamma \subset \mathrm{SU}(2) be a finite subgroup. Let X be the minimal resolution of \mathbb{C}^2 / \Gamma. The link M = S^3 / \Gamma is a compact 3-dimensional strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold. Equip M with the induced principal \mathrm{SU}(2)-bundle P \to M and the state bundle \mathcal{S} = P \times_{\mathrm{SU}(2)} \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}). This specifies an archimedean quantum observable universe.

The McKay correspondence classifies the subgroups \Gamma by ADE Dynkin diagrams. The exceptional divisors of X \to \mathbb{C}^2/\Gamma are copies of \mathbb{CP}^1 intersecting in the corresponding Dynkin pattern. Because S^3/\Gamma is connected, the aether parameter q is constant. The weight decomposition inherits the \Gamma-equivariant splitting of forms on S^3. The Reeb decomposition reduces to the Hopf fibration S^3/\Gamma \to S^2, with the Reeb vector field \xi generating the \mathrm{U}(1) fibre rotation.

This classification yields one quantum observable universe for each Dynkin type (A_n, D_n, E_6, E_7, E_8). The connection data derives from the instanton moduli space on X.
ex:instanton: Example Instanton connection. To verify that the categorical formalism recovers the classical gauge-theoretic object, the formalism is specialised to the archimedean setting. In the archimedean quantum universe, a categorical instanton specialises to an instanton connection on P. This is a connection A whose curvature F_A, restricted to H = \ker\varTheta, is self-dual: F_A|_H = {*_H}F_A|_H. The q-Hodge star \star_q specialises to the Tanaka–Webster Hodge star *_H on \Lambda^2 H^*. Consequently, \star_q-self-duality recovers classical *_H-self-duality.
ex:irreducible-connection:
Example Irreducibility of the connection. An instanton in the archimedean regime cannot reduce to an abelian \mathrm{U}(1) sub-bundle. Its gauge orbit must remain free. This geometric fact specialises the categorical irreducibility axiom: every instanton connection A on P is irreducible.

The vanishing cohomology H^0(M, \mathrm{Ad}(P)) = 0 provides the archimedean instance of \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0. Concretely, a non-zero section s \in H^0(M, \mathrm{Ad}(P)) furnishes an \mathrm{Ad}-invariant direction in \mathfrak{su}(2) at every point. This reduces the connection to \mathrm{U}(1). The QOU vanishing axiom forbids this, forcing the gauge orbit of A to be free.
ex:self-dual-curvature:
Example Self-duality of the curvature. On a four-dimensional space, the Yang–Mills energy splits into a topological floor, fixed by the bundle's second Chern number, and a non-negative remainder that measures the anti-self-dual part of the curvature. A connection attains the floor precisely when its curvature is self-dual. This example specialises categorical self-duality to recover the classical instanton picture.

In an archimedean quantum observable universe with \dim_{\mathbb{R}} H = 4, categorical self-duality specialises: every instanton connection A on P satisfies F_A|_H = {*_H}F_A|_H, where *_H denotes the Hodge star on the four-dimensional space H. Under the same specialisation, the categorical Yang–Mills functional \int_A(\star_q(F_\nabla) \cdot F_\nabla) becomes the ordinary Yang–Mills energy \int_M \lVert F_A|_H \rVert^2\varTheta \wedge (d\varTheta)^2 of the restricted curvature F_A|_H on the base M.

The Bogomolny trick decomposes \lVert F_A|_H \rVert^2 = \lVert F_A^+ \rVert^2 + \lVert F_A^- \rVert^2 into its self-dual and anti-self-dual pieces. The self-dual part \int \lVert F_A^+ \rVert^2 is a topological invariant (the second Chern number c_2(P)) and cannot be lowered. The anti-self-dual part carries energy with no such topological floor. Minimising the Yang–Mills functional forces F_A^-|_H = 0.
ex:reeb-decomposition:
Example Reeb decomposition. In the archimedean realisation, the categorical weight decomposition specialises to the Reeb decomposition. The contact form \varTheta canonically separates the \mathrm{U}(1)-fibre direction from the base, so the weight grading becomes a split of forms into vertical and horizontal parts. Let \xi denote the Reeb vector field, characterised by \iota_\xi d\varTheta = 0 and \varTheta(\xi) = 1. Every differential k-form \alpha (k \geq 1) on M decomposes uniquely as

  \alpha = \alpha_H + \varTheta \wedge \iota_\xi\alpha,

where \alpha_H := \alpha - \varTheta \wedge \iota_\xi\alpha is the horizontal component (\iota_\xi\alpha_H = 0) and \alpha_V := \varTheta \wedge \iota_\xi\alpha is the vertical component. The Reeb vector \xi generates the \mathrm{U}(1)-action (the maximal torus). The weight-0 subspace is the horizontal distribution H = \ker\varTheta.
ex:cosmological-limits:
Example Cosmological limits of q. Conjectural interpretation. The parameter range of the aether field q models a cosmological trajectory for a quantum observable universe. The limits of q represent a "big bang" and a "heat death".

Consider M = S^3 equipped with the standard contact form \varTheta and the standard instanton on the Hopf bundle. As the instanton curvature concentrates near a point p_0 \in S^3, the aether field q partitions into two regimes:

  • Near p_0 (q(p) \to \infty, \hbar_q \to 1): Uncertainty becomes maximal ([\hat{X},\hat{P}]_q \to J). Observables become maximally non-commutative. The quantum observable universe becomes fully quantum-mechanical, retaining no classical shadow. This is the "big bang" regime.

  • Away from p_0 (q(p) \to 1, \hbar_q \to 0): The commutator [\hat{X}, \hat{P}]_q vanishes. The Hopf algebra becomes cocommutative (\sigma \circ \Delta = \Delta). Observations commute, q-deformed operators reduce to their classical limits, and the transport equation reduces to classical parallel transport (\nabla\psi = 0). This is the "heat death" regime: a fully classical, frozen universe.

At both limits, the quantum observable universe structure degenerates:

  • As q \to \infty, the Frobenius pairing \langle f, g \rangle = \int_A(\mu(f \otimes g)) loses non-degeneracy. Axiom (1) of the definition of a quantum observable universe fails. The universe ceases to be observable.

  • As q \to 1, the q-Hodge star \star_q reduces to the classical Hodge star \star_1. The quantum gauge group \mathrm{SU}_q(2) collapses to the classical Lie group \mathrm{SU}(2). The deformation vanishes, and the aether parameter carries no information.

The conjecture is that the physically meaningful regime strictly satisfies 1 < q < \infty, where quantum and classical features coexist. Rigorously analyzing these limits requires controlling the singular behavior of the Frobenius form as q \to \infty. This remains an open problem.
sec:categorical-differential-bridge-prea:
The Archimedean Hartree computations of Part III require a positive-definite inner product on fibre states. Because a braided monoidal category over a general ground ring R carries only the bilinear Frobenius pairing \int_A, an inner product must be constructed from the contact geometry of the Archimedean base.

This section builds that metric by extracting the complex structure from the Levi form of the CR aether, pairing it with the contact one-form to form the Tanaka–Webster inner product, and transporting the resulting Hilbert-space pairing back across the fibre functor \tau. Readers concerned solely with algebraic identities over \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}] may treat this differential bridge as an external evaluation map that becomes active only at the Archimedean wall.
rem:c-aether-via-levi:
Remark Archimedean aether via the Levi form. The abstract aether parameter q measures a connection's departure from classicality. Its concrete archimedean realisation follows.

Let A be an instanton connection on P. Let F_A^+ be its self-dual curvature. Let L_\varTheta(V, W) = -id\varTheta(V, \bar{W}) be the Levi form. Because \Lambda^{1,1} H^* \subset \Lambda^+ H^* on the 4-dimensional distribution H, the Tanaka–Webster metric and Killing form define a natural contraction \langle L_\varTheta, F_A^+\rangle_p \in \mathbb{R}. The categorical aether parameter over \mathbb{C} or \mathbb{R} evaluates to the smooth field

  q(p) = 1 + \bigl\lvert\langle L_\varTheta, F_A^+ \rangle\bigr\rvert(p),
  \qquad p \in M.

When the connection is classical (F_A^+ = 0), q = 1. In the deep-quantum regime, q \to \infty.

All downstream quantities (\hbar_q, commutators, Yang–Mills action) are algebraic in q. Replacing 1 + x with \exp(x) does not change the structural theory. The algebraic formula 1+x is used because it remains well-defined over an arbitrary base ring R. Non-archimedean analogues appear in subsequent chapters.
sec:webster-inner-product:
Tanaka–Webster inner product notation.

The inner product induced by the Tanaka–Webster metric g_\varTheta [tanaka1974, tanaka1975, webster1978] on the horizontal distribution H = \ker\varTheta and its exterior powers is denoted \langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle_\varTheta. For vector fields X, Y and differential forms \alpha, \beta:

  \langle X, Y \rangle_\varTheta := g_\varTheta(X, Y),
  \qquad
  \langle \alpha, \beta \rangle_\varTheta := g_\varTheta(\alpha^{\sharp}, \beta^{\sharp}).

This notation makes several dualities visually transparent:

  • Reeb duality. The Reeb vector field \xi is the metric dual to the contact form \varTheta: \varTheta(X) = \langle \xi, X \rangle_\varTheta for all X.
  • Adjoint definition. The q-codifferential \delta_q is uniquely characterised by \langle d_q\alpha, \beta \rangle_\varTheta = \langle \alpha, \delta_q\beta \rangle_\varTheta.
  • Aether contraction. The natural contraction \langle L_\varTheta, F_A^+ \rangle appearing in the aether parameter is exactly the inner product \langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle_\varTheta extended to bundle-valued 2-forms.
rem:observation-archimedean: Remark Archimedean realisation of observation. Observing the universe changes it. The aether parameter q(p) is perturbed by condition (2). Every observation shifts the non-commutative geometry. In the archimedean realisation, an observation is a continuous open map from the spacetime base M to the bundle of endomorphisms \mathrm{End}(\mathcal{S}) \to M, encoding the coordinate change in torsion energy of the bundle \mathcal{S}.
def:spatial-realization-functor:
Definition Spatial realization functor. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe. The spatial realization of A is the space

  M = \mathrm{Spec}(A) = \{ p \colon \mathbf{1} \to A \mid
  p \text{ is a categorical point} \},

equipped with the following structures in \mathbf{C}:

  1. for each point p, the augmentation ideal \mathfrak{m}_p = \ker(p^* \colon A \to \mathbf{1});
  2. the contact form \varTheta_A \in \Omega^1(A), induced by the Frobenius form \int_A \colon A \to \mathbf{1} via pullback along the universal derivation d \colon A \to \Omega^1(A);
  3. the Reeb derivation \xi, the generator of the maximal torus action.
rem:spatial-realization-functor-remark:
Remark The spatial realization as a contact manifold. The spatial realization realises the algebra A as a contact manifold. It sends the Frobenius form to the global contact 1-form and the torus generator to the Reeb field. The target M is an ordinary smooth manifold—the classical space whose function algebra C^\infty(M) the fibre functor \tau recovers from A. Its structures are derived purely within \mathbf{C}:

  1. Local germs. The augmentation ideal \mathfrak{m}_p captures the functions vanishing at p. The quotient \mathfrak{m}_p / \mathfrak{m}_p^2 is functorially dual to the tangent space T_p M. This gives the first-order germ decomposition

      A / \mathfrak{m}_p^2
   \cong 
  \mathbf{1} \oplus \mathfrak{m}_p / \mathfrak{m}_p^2.

  2. Kähler differentials. The module \Omega^1(A) of Kähler differentials exists in \mathbf{C} by hypothesis. Under the fibre functor, \tau(\Omega^1(A)) maps to sections of the cotangent bundle \Gamma(T^* M).

  3. The Reeb derivation. The generator \xi satisfies the Cartan relations \iota_\xi \varTheta_A = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{1}} and \iota_\xi d\varTheta_A = 0 within the non-commutative differential calculus.

\begin{equation}\label{eq:spatial-realization-diagram}
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
  A \ar[r, "\tau"] \ar[d, "d"']
  & C^{\infty}(M) \ar[d, "d"] \\
  \Omega^1(A) \ar[r, "\tau"']
  & \Gamma(T^* M)
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
  \varTheta_A \ar[r, mapsto, "\tau"]
  & \varTheta \\
  \xi \ar[r, mapsto, "\tau"']
  & \xi_{\mathrm{Reeb}}
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad\text{(spatial realisation)}
\end{equation}

Under \tau, these algebraic objects map to their geometric counterparts. \varTheta_A becomes the global contact 1-form \varTheta. \xi becomes the Reeb vector field. Non-degeneracy of \int_A guarantees that d\varTheta is maximally non-degenerate on \ker\varTheta, which defines a contact manifold.
rem:spatial-realization-base-generality:
Remark The base of the spatial realisation: the properties used and the case excluded. The spatial realisation functor states that its target M = \mathrm{Spec}(A) is an ordinary smooth manifold. That is an assertion of the definition, not a consequence of the axioms, and it is worth separating the two: which properties of M the constructions of this paper use, and which are decoration.

What is used. Four properties, each a property of the algebra A in \mathbf{C} rather than of a manifold.

  1. The points. M is the set of categorical points p \colon \mathbf{1} \to A, and the local germ A/\mathfrak{m}_{p}^{2} \cong \mathbf{1} \oplus \mathfrak{m}_{p}/\mathfrak{m}_{p}^{2} at p is Zariski's description of a tangent space; it makes sense for any commutative algebra and gives a vector space of constant dimension exactly when A is regular.
  2. The one-forms. The module \Omega^{1}(A) of Kähler differentials exists by hypothesis, and the constructions use that \tau(\Omega^{1}(A)) is the module of sections of a bundle — that is, that \Omega^{1}(A) is a dualisable object of \mathbf{C} of constant rank. For a finitely generated algebra over a field, \Omega^{1}(A) finitely generated projective of rank \dim A is equivalent to smoothness [hartshorne-1977]; it is the same hypothesis under which the Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg theorem identifies Hochschild homology with differential forms [hkr-1962].
  3. The contact form \varTheta_{A}, which needs only \Omega^{1}(A), the Frobenius form and the universal derivation.
  4. The Reeb derivation, which needs a torus action and the contraction \iota_{\xi} on \Omega^{1}(A).

Nothing uses a topology on M, a partition of unity, or the real numbers.

What can therefore replace "smooth manifold". Any base on which \Omega^{1}(A) is dualisable of constant rank: a smooth affine variety over a field, which is the case of the finite-field models of a later section of this chapter; a formal scheme, when A is completed at a point; a smooth rigid-analytic space, for the p-adic models; a supermanifold, when A is \mathbb{Z}/2-graded; or a quotient stack [M/G] when A carries the action of a finite group such as the S_{5} of Bring's curve, in which case the categorical points of the invariant subalgebra are the orbits. The proofs of this chapter go through verbatim in each case, because they never leave the category \mathbf{C}. The word "manifold" fixes the real-analytic case for exposition and is the case in which the physical interpretation is made; it is not what the theorems require.

The singular base. The one case the constructions exclude is a base whose Kähler module fails to be projective. The affine cone over Bring's curve is such a base: away from the vertex it is smooth, but at the vertex the fibre of \mathfrak{m}_{p}/\mathfrak{m}_{p}^{2} jumps to the dimension of the ambient space, \Omega^{1} is not locally free, and the Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg identification fails. The link of that vertex — the boundary of a small neighbourhood of it — is a three-manifold fibred by circles over the curve with Euler number 2 - 2g = -6 [orlik-wagreich1971], whose fundamental group is infinite; a quaternionic model of the cone describes the smooth fibre near a point of the curve, not this link. The phrase "ordinary smooth manifold" therefore has a single function in the definition: it excludes the vertex. Stated as the categorical condition, that exclusion is a checkable hypothesis, and the generality of the previous paragraph follows without further work.
prop:categorical-archimedean-bridge:
Proposition Categorical--geometric correspondence. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with weight decomposition \pi_H, \pi_V and categorical q-exterior derivative d_q.

Under the fibre functor \tau, the categorical and geometric definitions of d_q coincide. The categorical vertical derivative \pi_V \circ d corresponds to the geometric operation of contracting with the Reeb vector field \xi and wedging with the contact form \varTheta. This correspondence forms a commuting square:

\begin{equation}\label{eq:categorical-archimedean-bridge-diagram}
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
  \Omega^k(A) \ar[r, "\pi_V \circ d"] \ar[d, "\tau"']
  & \Omega^{k+1}(A) \ar[d, "\tau"] \\
  \Omega^k(M) \ar[r, "\varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi"']
  & \Omega^{k+1}(M)
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad\text{(categorical--geometric bridge)}
\end{equation}

This states that \tau(\pi_V \circ d) = \varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi, where \varTheta is the contact form and \mathcal{L}_\xi is the Lie derivative along the Reeb vector field.
prf:categorical-archimedean-bridge:
Proof The claim is that the image of the categorical differential d_q under the fibre functor \tau equals the archimedean q-exterior derivative.

The functor \tau dictates the following geometric correspondences:

  • The Frobenius form \int_A maps to the contact integral \int_M \alpha \wedge (d\varTheta)^n.
  • The maximal torus generator \xi maps to the Reeb vector field, satisfying \iota_\xi\varTheta = 1 and \iota_\xi d\varTheta = 0.
  • The categorical weight decomposition \pi_H, \pi_V maps to the geometric splitting \Omega^k(M) = \Omega^k_H(M) \oplus \varTheta \wedge \Omega^{k-1}_H(M) determined by the Reeb direction.

Let \alpha \in \Omega^k(M) be a differential form. The vertical projection \pi_V(d\alpha) isolates the component of d\alpha with non-zero weight under the T-action. Geometrically, this T-action is the Reeb flow \phi_t \colon M \to M generated by the Lie derivative \mathcal{L}_\xi. The non-zero-weight component lies entirely along the Reeb direction:

  \pi_V(d\alpha) = \varTheta \wedge \iota_\xi(d\alpha)
  = \varTheta \wedge (\mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha - d(\iota_\xi\alpha)).

For horizontal forms (\iota_\xi\alpha = 0), this simplifies to \varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha. For arbitrary forms, write \alpha = \alpha_H + \varTheta \wedge \beta. Because \mathcal{L}_\xi\varTheta = 0, the identity \pi_V(d\alpha) = \varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha holds in all cases. Hence

  \tau(d_q) = q^{-1} d + (1 - q^{-1})\varTheta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi,

which matches the archimedean definition of d_q (archimedean q-exterior derivative).
rem:physicist-translation:
Remark Archimedean realization of the categorical action. In the archimedean realization where \mathbf{C} = \mathbf{Vect}_{\mathbb{R}}, A = C^{\infty}(M) for a Riemannian manifold M, and \nabla is an Ehresmann connection on a principal G-bundle P \to M, the three constituents of the categorical action acquire their classical meanings:

  1. The categorical trace \mathrm{tr} = \mathrm{ev}_A \circ (\mathrm{id}_{A^\vee} \otimes {-}) \circ \mathrm{coev}_A becomes integration against the volume form: \mathrm{tr}(\cdot) \to \int_M (\cdot)\mathrm{dvol}.
  2. The Lagrangian endomorphism \Phi_q = \mathcal{L}_q becomes the Lagrangian density \mathscr{L}(x), a section of the density bundle.
  3. The categorical Dirac operator \mathcal{D}_\nabla reduces to the gauge-covariant Dirac operator D\!\!\!\!/ = \gamma^\mu D_\mu.

The three-term decomposition then reads

  \mathfrak{S}_q
   \longrightarrow 
  \frac{1}{16\pi G}\!\int_M R\mathrm{dvol}
  - 
  \frac{1}{4g^2}\!\int_M \mathrm{Tr}(F \wedge \star F)
  + 
  \int_M \bar\psi D\!\!\!\!/\psi\mathrm{dvol},

the Einstein–Hilbert + Yang–Mills + Dirac action, with q \to 1. The coupling constants G, g emerge from the normalization of the Frobenius form \int_A and the aether parameter q respectively. They are not free parameters of the categorical theory. They are determined by the choice of archimedean realization.
rem:categorical-action-vs-chern-simons:
Remark Comparison with the classical Chern--Simons action. The classical Chern–Simons action [witten1988]

  S_{\mathrm{CS}}[A_{\mathrm{cl}}]
  =
  \frac{k}{4\pi}\!\int_M \mathrm{Tr}\!\left(
    A_{\mathrm{cl}} \wedge dA_{\mathrm{cl}}
    + \tfrac{2}{3}\, A_{\mathrm{cl}} \wedge A_{\mathrm{cl}} \wedge A_{\mathrm{cl}}
  \right)

and the categorical action \mathfrak{S} = \mathrm{tr}(\Phi) share a common skeleton. Both are scalar functionals built by tracing an internal morphism. (Here A_{\mathrm{cl}} is a \mathfrak{g}-valued connection 1-form on a 3-manifold M, distinct from the QOU observable object A \in \mathbf{C}.) They diverge in their encoding of integration and trace:

Chern–Simons Categorical
Domain 3-manifold M rigid monoidal (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)
Integration \int_M \{-\} \mathrm{ev}_A \circ (\mathrm{id}_{A^\vee} \otimes \{-\}) \circ \mathrm{coev}_A
Trace Lie-algebra \mathrm{Tr}_{\mathfrak{g}} categorical (rigid) trace on A
Dynamics explicit A_{\mathrm{cl}} \wedge dA_{\mathrm{cl}} + \tfrac{2}{3} A_{\mathrm{cl}}^{\wedge 3} packaged inside \Phi \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A)

In the archimedean limit, the trace becomes \int_M \{-\}\,\mathrm{dvol}. The rigid loop closure \mathrm{ev}_A \circ \{-\} \circ \mathrm{coev}_A yields spacetime integration without an independently postulated volume form. The rigid structure supplies it. The perturbative expansion A_{\mathrm{cl}} = A_{\mathrm{cl}}^{(0)} + \mathcal{A} around a flat connection corresponds to fixing a background categorical connection and expanding \Phi_q = \mathcal{D}_\nabla^2 + \cdots in fluctuations.

The bulk categorical action does not recover classical Chern–Simons. The archimedean image of \mathfrak{S}_q = \mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{L}_q) is the sum of the Einstein–Hilbert, Yang–Mills, and Dirac actions. Classical Chern–Simons enters the framework separately as a geometric knot invariant for non-hyperbolic torus knots.
sec:non-archimedean-models-preamble:
Archimedean models realise the aether parameter q as a smoothly varying real or complex number, so they see the aether only through its differential-geometric shadow. This picture does not record the arithmetic of the q-commutation data itself—its integral form and its behaviour in positive characteristic. Recovering that structure requires completions carrying a non-archimedean valuation, in which q is p-adic rather than continuous.

The concrete phenomenon these models expose is a lifting problem. The question is whether the aether can be reconstructed from the algebra generated by its infinitesimal q-commutation relations. The Heisenberg uncertainty relation—read as the q-commutator [\hat{X},\hat{P}]_q = i\hbar_q—is the germ to be lifted. This construction is traced from the enveloping algebras onward, through the Lusztig integral form and its q-deformed PBW basis to the p-adic and finite-field realisations.
sec:enveloping-algebras-models:
The Heisenberg uncertainty relation, [\hat{X},\hat{P}]_q = i\hbar_q, provides a single physical q-commutator between position and momentum. The enveloping-algebra construction generalizes this germ to reconstruct the full aether from its infinitesimal q-commutation data.

This lifting problem is solved using the Lusztig integral form of \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)), its triangular decomposition, and the q-deformed Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt (PBW) basis. The integral form and triangular decomposition factor the generators into component subalgebras. The q-deformed PBW basis provides an explicit ordered basis for the enveloping algebra. Together, these algebraic structures lift the infinitesimal q-commutation relations back to the aether.
ex:p-adic-realisation:
Example \mathbb{Q}_\pp realisation. To show that the aether parameter and the surrounding categorical apparatus are not tied to an archimedean base field, the archimedean tuple is realised over a p-adic base. Let k = \mathbb{Q}_p and let \mathbf{C} be the category of F-isocrystals over \mathbb{Q}_p. This is a \mathbb{Q}_p-linear rigid monoidal category. The quantum group \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2)) base-changed to \mathbb{Q}_p provides a Frobenius–Hopf object A, where the Frobenius form \int_A arises from the p-adic Haar measure. The Frobenius endomorphism \varphi on \mathbf{C} plays the role of the Levi-form contraction. The categorical aether parameter specialises to q = p^{-v_p(\det\varphi)} \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}) \cong \mathbb{Q}_p. The fibre functor \tau is the forgetful functor to \mathrm{Vect}_{\mathbb{Q}_p}. The observability condition \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 amounts to the irreducibility of the associated F-crystal, generalising irreducible connection to the p-adic setting.

Key structures.

  • The classical Frobenius integrability theorem constrains q-torsion leaves to be Legendrian. Over \mathbb{Q}_p, this is replaced by compatibility of the connection with the Frobenius lift. A connection that underlies an F-crystal is integrable by construction: crystals correspond to modules with integrable, topologically nilpotent connection [andre-baldassarri2002]. Being unit-root is a further condition, and unit-root F-crystals correspond to continuous \mathbb{Z}_p-representations of the fundamental group (Katz; see [andre-baldassarri2002]).
  • Crystal cohomology (de Rham–Witt complex) plays the role of de Rham cohomology.
  • The base-field-independent quantum universe and quantum observable universe provide the categorical framework via Tannakian reconstruction.
sec:witt-vector-lifting: The \mathbb{Q}_p realisation provides a QOU over characteristic 0. The \mathbb{F}_p realisation provides one over characteristic p. The Witt vector functor W and the theory of formal groups over p-adic rings mediate the passage between them.
def:witt-vector-lift:
Definition Witt vector lift of a formal group. Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p, let W(k) be its ring of Witt vectors, and let \varphi\colon W(k)\to k be the reduction map. Let H be a formal group law over k. A Witt vector lift of H is a formal group law G over W(k), of the same dimension, whose base change along \varphi is H:

G \otimes_{W(k),\,\varphi} k \;=\; H .

If G is commutative then so is its reduction. The definition asserts nothing about existence or uniqueness of a lift, and it does not involve a Poisson structure.
prop:skew-poisson-integration:
Proposition Integration of skewed-Poisson structures. Let k be a field and let \{H_i, H\} be a commutative geometric formal group over k (Leitner, Definition 3.1). Let T be the splay of the distribution algebras A_i = \mathrm{Dist}(H_i), and let \pi be a Poisson structure on T that is both strongly filtered and strongly multiplicative (Definition 1.11: the comultiplication of T induced from the A_i satisfies the strong-multiplicativity identity with respect to \pi). Let J \subset T be the ideal generated by the elements fg - gf - \pi(f, g) with f, g \in T, and put

U \;=\; T / J.

Then (Leitner, Theorem 3.7) U is the distribution algebra \mathrm{Dist}(G) of a formal group G over k, and \{H_i, G\} is a geometric formal group.
prf:skew-poisson-integration:
Proof Proof of Integration of skewed-Poisson structures. The proof of Theorem 3.7 in Leitner (arXiv:math/0602138) has two parts.

  1. Bialgebra structure. Theorem 1.9 shows that U \cong \bigotimes_i A_i as k-modules for a fixed ordering of the index set. Its proof exhibits a Gröbner basis of the defining ideal, made of the relations f_{i,j} of the A_i and the elements g_{a,b} = ab - ba - \tilde\pi(a, b); this step uses only that \pi is strongly filtered. Proposition 1.13 then uses strong multiplicativity to show that \Delta vanishes on the g_{a,b}, so the comultiplication descends to an algebra map U \to U \otimes U.
  2. Divided-power structure. With the bialgebra structure in hand, the proof writes \Delta on ordered monomials \delta_x^J using Remark 3.2 and checks that U carries the DVPS structure of a distribution algebra.

Both parts hold for one-dimensional H_i over any commutative ring, under the additional hypothesis that the counit of T kills \pi. Part 1 follows the Gröbner–Shirshov route: the ordered monomials form a basis of U, the normal monomials are the words whose blocks strictly increase, and these are in bijection with multi-indices J; the coproduct and counit of the splay descend to U. Part 2 builds a formal group law G from the basis by Cartier reconstruction, with the product of U equal to the convolution of G. Whether \{H_i, G\} forms a geometric formal group is left open.
rem:witt-lift-qou:
Remark Role in the QOU lifting theorem. The skew-Poisson integration theorem is a statement over a field k of characteristic p. Its bearing on the p-adic realisation is limited, and this remark records what it does and does not supply.

  1. It supplies a construction over k: from a strongly filtered, strongly multiplicative Poisson structure on the splay of the distribution algebras of a commutative geometric formal group, it builds a bialgebra U with a PBW basis, which the source identifies with \mathrm{Dist}(G) for a non-commutative formal group G over k.
  2. It does not supply a Witt vector lift. No lift of G or of H to W(k) or \mathbb{Z}_p is constructed in the source, so the passage from the \mathbb{F}_p fibre algebra to a \mathbb{Q}_p fibre algebra is not a consequence of it.
  3. Strong multiplicativity is a compatibility between \pi and the comultiplication of the free product. It is not the Frobenius relation (\mathrm{Id}\otimes m)\circ(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{Id}) = \Delta\circ m used in jet prolongation, and the theorem does not prove that relation.

No unit-root F-crystal criterion for integrability appears in the source.
sec:finite-fields-intro:
Finite fields provide an independent check on the axioms. They reproduce the knot-theoretic and Frobenius structure of the archimedean models in characteristic p.

Let q range over \mathbb{F}_p^{\times}, or a primitive \ell-th root of unity in \overline{\mathbb{F}}_p with \ell coprime to p. The categorical data forms a fusion category with finitely many simple objects. The \mathbb{F}_p realisation constructs \mathrm{Rep}_{\mathbb{F}_p}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) as a QOU. The regular representation satisfies the Frobenius and observability axioms. This supplies the finite-field counterpart to the Calabi–Yau and Bring's-surface witnesses.

Comparison with characteristic zero proceeds through reduction from \mathbb{Q}_p to \mathbb{F}_p, finite-group representation theory, and Betti-number matching. The universal R-matrix of U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) at a root of unity yields the Jones polynomial J_K(q) via the Markov trace. This recovers the knot-theoretic output of the archimedean models.

This compatibility sets up the rigidity-pairing narrative of the next section, which examines Mostow confinement and the archimedean wall.
ex:finite-field-realisation:
Example \mathbb{F}_\pp realisation. The finite field setting demonstrates that the Frobenius non-degeneracy and observability conditions do not depend on characteristic zero or archimedean structure.

Fix a prime p and set k = \mathbb{F}_p. Let \mathbf{C} = \mathrm{Rep}_{\mathbb{F}_p}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) be the category of finite-dimensional representations of the quantum group \mathrm{SU}_q(2) over \mathbb{F}_p. Here q \in \mathbb{F}_p^{\times}. More generally, let q \in \overline{\mathbb{F}}_p be a primitive \ell-th root of unity, with \ell coprime to p. Then \mathbf{C} extends to a fusion category over \mathbb{F}_p(q) with finitely many simple objects.

The regular representation provides the Frobenius–Hopf object A. The forgetful functor to \mathrm{Vect}_{\mathbb{F}_p} provides the fibre functor \tau. Semisimplicity of the fusion category guarantees the non-degeneracy of the Frobenius form \int_A. The observability condition \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 holds for q \neq 1, as the trivial representation does not appear as a summand of the adjoint representation.
sec:jones-polynomials:
Jones polynomials bridge the finite-field models of this section and the categorical machinery.

The fusion category \mathrm{Rep}_{\mathbb{F}_p}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) carries a canonical R-matrix. This arises from the universal R-matrix of U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) specialised at a primitive \ell-th root of unity in \overline{\mathbb{F}}_p. This R-matrix promotes the fundamental representation V to a braided object. The braid group B_n acts on V^{\otimes n}. The Markov trace then produces a knot invariant. Following standard Reshetikhin–Turaev normalisation, this yields the Jones polynomial J_K(q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}] modulo p.

The knot crossing number counts the R-matrix applications. Thus J_K(q) is a polynomial of degree bounded by the crossing number. The Hecke algebra structure constants control its coefficients. At a root of unity q = \zeta_\ell, divisibility patterns of J_K(q) encode the modular-Hecke combinatorics.

The p-adic (Witt-vector) lift of the aether parameter recovers the Jones polynomial by reducing the lifted R-matrix modulo p. The modular Jones invariant agrees with the characteristic-zero invariant where both are defined. The finite-field and archimedean models thus produce identical knot-theoretic output.
